title: Gas Station
hints: first check: is a solution even possible? compare total gas to total cost
if you simulate starting from station 0 and your tank goes negative at station k, could any station between 0 and k have been a valid start?
no - if station 0 could not reach station k+1 with a full tank, no station after 0 and before k+1 could either, since they'd arrive at k with even less surplus fuel than starting from 0 would have
so whenever the running tank drops below 0, discard every station tried so far as a candidate start and try the very next station, resetting the tank to 0
if total gas >= total cost, the station where you last reset the candidate start is guaranteed to be the unique valid answer - you never need to double check it separately
commonMistakes: restarting the search from station 0 again after a failure instead of just moving the candidate start forward by one and continuing the same pass
assuming a station with gas[i] < cost[i] can never be the start, when actually the deciding factor is the running total, not any single station's local balance
forgetting the upfront feasibility check and returning a station index even when total gas is less than total cost

content.problemStatement:
There are `n` gas stations arranged in a circle. `gas[i]` is the amount
of fuel available at station `i`, and `cost[i]` is the fuel needed to
drive from station `i` to station `(i+1) mod n`. You start with an empty
tank at some station of your choosing and drive around the circle in
one direction.

**Return the index of the starting station that lets you complete the full circuit without running out of fuel, or -1 if none does.**

You can assume that if a solution exists, exactly one starting station works.
notes: total gas exactly equals total cost (a solution must exist)
total gas is less than total cost (answer is -1)
a single station (trivially the answer if gas[0] >= cost[0])
the valid starting index is the last one in the array

total gas (9) is less than total cost (10), so no starting point can complete the circuit
